IR.rationale: A steepening curve with no rise in short rates signals better growth expectations without monetary tightening, which favours equity returns. The term-spread literature links a steeper curve to improving growth and higher risk premia.

B.rationale: Narrowing Baa spreads together with strong high-yield returns describe easing credit conditions. Credit markets often lead equities because they price default risk and the funding conditions of firms.

V.rationale: High implied volatility carries a large variance and equity risk premium, so subsequent equity returns tend to be higher on average.

AP.rationale: Strong emerging-market equity returns proxy for global risk appetite and growth momentum, which spill over into US equity returns.

ST.rationale: High reversal-factor returns mean liquidity providers are being well paid. That happens when liquidity is scarce, and such states tend to be followed by higher market returns.

FX.rationale: A rising Australian dollar and a weakening yen mark a risk-on carry environment that coincides with rising global risk appetite.

COM.rationale: Oil price changes have been documented to predict equity returns negatively with a lag, because markets underreact to the cost shock that oil represents.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions raise required risk premia, so expected returns are higher once stress is priced in.

ENDG.rationale: Recent index performance relative to its history captures short-horizon continuation or reversal at the index level.

IR.rationale: Falling bill yields with bull steepening reflect flight to quality and expected easing, which typically accompanies rising equity turbulence.

B.rationale: Widening spreads with weak high-yield returns signal credit stress. Through the leverage channel, credit stress feeds into future equity variance.

V.rationale: Implied volatility contains forward-looking information about future variance beyond what recent realised variance already shows.

AP.rationale: Through the leverage and volatility-feedback effect, negative market returns raise future volatility more than positive returns do.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes tend to occur in turbulent markets, so weak momentum returns mark unstable, high-variance regimes.

FX.rationale: A strengthening yen with a weakening Australian dollar indicates carry unwinding and safe-haven flows, which are associated with rising risk across asset classes.

COM.rationale: Falling broad commodity prices signal global demand weakness, which tends to raise equity uncertainty.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress indicates funding and liquidity strain that amplifies equity volatility.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clusters, so high recent realised variance relative to its history carries residual persistence information.

IR.rationale: Falling bill yields with a steepening curve reflect flight to quality and expected easing in deteriorating conditions, a backdrop in which equity crashes are more likely.

B.rationale: Credit deterioration often precedes or accompanies equity drawdowns, because credit prices default risk first.

V.rationale: High implied volatility combined with high policy uncertainty widens the left tail of the return distribution.

AP.rationale: Weak recent market returns raise volatility through the leverage effect, which makes large subsequent losses more likely.

ST.rationale: Momentum underperformance marks turbulent, stressed regimes in which the probability of large market losses is elevated.

FX.rationale: Carry unwinding and safe-haven yen demand are classic risk-off signals that are associated with equity tail losses.

COM.rationale: Sharp oil declines can reflect global demand shocks and stress in the energy sector, which raise downside tail risk.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions combined with rising jobless claims signal both financial and real deterioration, which is a precursor of large losses.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent performance indicates a drawdown regime in which further large losses are more likely through volatility clustering.

IR.rationale: Falling short rates signal expected monetary easing, which can trigger strong equity rallies.

B.rationale: Credit spreads tightening alongside rebounding high-yield bonds signal relief after stress, a precondition for large equity gains.

V.rationale: High-volatility states widen both tails, and they also carry high risk premia that make large rebounds more likely.

AP.rationale: Strong emerging-market equities indicate broad global risk-on momentum that supports large US equity gains.

ST.rationale: High reversal returns indicate highly paid liquidity provision in dislocated markets, which tends to precede sharp rebounds.

FX.rationale: A rising Australian dollar signals improving global growth and risk appetite.

COM.rationale: Rising broad commodity prices reflect strengthening global demand, which is consistent with strong equity gains.

MC.rationale: Elevated stress raises both the dispersion of returns and expected returns, which makes large rebounds more probable.

ENDG.rationale: Large gains cluster after weak periods because index returns are more volatile and tend to reverse in those regimes.
